page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features a single dedicated vCPU mapped to one physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes a CPU cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 0.25 MB L2, and 45 MB L3. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-standard-1 operates in the lower performance tiers. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores of 1088.79 place it in the bottom 25% and 10% of tested servers, respectively. Memory bandwidth is limited, with uncached read speeds at 10.68 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.71 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server achieved a static web serving throughput of 1.21 GB/sec and processed 1.29 million Redis SET operations per second. Large language model inference on a small 135M model yielded 96.03 tokens per second for prompt processing and 41.77 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-1 represents a low-cost entry point for basic computing needs, though its resource density and performance-per-resource ratios are low. The primary tradeoff is its limited processing power and memory capacity, which restrict its utility for resource-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple scripting, development or testing environments, and low-traffic database operations that do not require high computational throughput or parallel processing.
